text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts originating from eu-north1 (gw-eun1) starting 1789989980. Error rate >= 8% for last 2m, latency p95 2.4s. Auto-escalating to oncall.
sam (oncall): on it. Paging @maria and @kevin. Any ongoing deploys to eu-north1?
kevin (eng-sre): not that I'm aware of. Watching gateway dashboards now. Seeing connection resets from gw-eun1 -> model-worker pool mw-eun1, lots of TLS handshake failures.
maria (runtime): logs show rapid conn opens then RST from backend. Also noticing NAT source port exhaustion metric rising on nat-eun1. Possible ephemeral port churn from many short-lived model sessions.
sam (oncall): ok, that could explain 502s. Customer impact? Tess, any support tickets?
tess (cust-suc): getting multiple alerts. Affected customers: 3 enterprise customers in EU region (search queries + chat endpoints). Response times up, some requests returning 502. I'm preparing a banner template.
ops-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC-80912 created and routed to platform-oncall.
maria (runtime): mitigation suggestion: enable sticky connection pooling on gw-eun1 to reduce new ephemeral port usage, and increase NAT port range on nat-eun1 as short-term. Also throttle heavy prefixes from a few noisy customers.
kevin (eng-sre): I can increase nat ephemeral port range but that's infra change — doing now via terraform apply (plan ok). ETA ~120s.
sam (oncall): Maria, can we apply gateway-level pooling quick fix?
maria (runtime): yes. Pushing a runtime config patch to gw-eun1:
```
# runtime patch
pooling.conn_keepalive=true
pooling.max_per_route=100
```
Applying to cluster subset (canary) first.
kevin (eng-sre): nat range bumped from 15000-61000 -> 10000-65000, applied. Correlating metrics... ephemeral_port_free increased.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: runtime config rollout started on gw-eun1 (canary -> 10% nodes).
maria (runtime): canary looks good, error rates dropping on those nodes from 9.2% -> 1.8%. Rolling to 100% now.
sam (oncall): good. While we stabilize, should we steer new user traffic to eu-west to reduce customer impact? That would be safer for critical customers.
jess (product): yes, please. We should avoid any data-plane differences; eu-west has same model versions. Approve steering.
kevin (eng-sre): starting traffic steering: updating edge policy to prefer eu-west for non-region-bound traffic and adding sticky header to keep active sessions. Command: `rbctl route update --from eu-north1 --prefer eu-west1 --weight 80`
ops-bot: Edge control: route update accepted, propagation expected ~45s.
tess (cust-suc): banner ready: "We are mitigating elevated errors in EU-North, traffic is being redirected; some requests may see slightly higher latency. Engineering is actively addressing." Sending to affected customers in 15m unless we clear sooner.
maria (runtime): monitoring: error rate across eu-north1 now trending down to 0.9% after full rollout. Latency p95 back to 1.1s. NAT port exhaustion resolved.
sam (oncall): nice work. Remaining actions: 1) keep steering for 5 more mins to ensure no residual backlog; 2) run connection pool audit; 3) schedule postmortem if any root causes remain.
kevin (eng-sre): creating follow-up runbook issue and tagging infra for permanent NAT tuning + connection reuse improvements.
jess (product): high-level note for customers: brief summary + ETA for postmortem by EOD.
tess (cust-suc): I'll hold off on banner if we keep improving; will notify customers at 15m if not resolved.
ops-bot: Incident INC-80912: status -> mitigated. Resolution notes: connection pooling config applied; NAT ephemeral range increased; traffic steered to eu-west temporarily.
sam (oncall): handoff to oncall-sre for monitoring window. @kevin please own the post-incident follow-ups.
maria (runtime): will add logs + heap snapshot analysis to the postmortem. Initial hypothesis: sudden increase in short-lived model sessions (prefix fanout) causing NAT port churn and backend TLS resets -> gateway 5xx.
sam (oncall): closing thread here; will reopen if we see re-escalation. Good job team :thumbsup:
